reasoning: The image shows a corn plant with massive black, powdery/sooty fungal masses replacing the ear/tassel tissue. The characteristic dark teliospore masses with visible fibrous host tissue remnants, located at the ear/tassel position, are diagnostic of head smut (Sphacelotheca reiliana). This differs from common smut which produces galls on various plant parts, while head smut specifically destroys the ear and tassel, replacing them with black spore masses enclosed in a membrane that breaks down to reveal the dark powdery spores mixed with host tissue strands.
